learning.focus: Make a cohesive raw basil sauce by crushing gently and adding oil last.
learning.outcome: A fragrant green sauce with finely worked leaves and nuts, evenly mixed cheeses and no loose pool of oil.
before: Choose fresh Genovese basil and weigh the leaves without stalks; wash and dry thoroughly.
Use a clean mortar with room for the pestle; additional loads extend active time as the recipe is increased.

Grate both cheeses before starting. Fiore Sardo is the Sardinian sheep’s-milk cheese in this formula. The sauce contains dairy and pine nuts; ingredient labels matter for allergen and rennet requirements.

checkpoints.cue: The leaves have become an even green paste without the mortar mixture feeling warm.
checkpoints.why: Steady gentle crushing gives a cohesive sauce while avoiding prolonged warm processing.

checkpoints.cue: The oil is worked into a creamy sauce without a separate puddle.
checkpoints.why: Adding it gradually after the solids lets you control the finished consistency.

troubleshooting.problem: The pesto is too stiff to coat pasta.
troubleshooting.cause: The concentrated sauce needs loosening for service.
troubleshooting.fix: Off the heat, stir a little reserved pasta water into only the portion being served, then toss. Do not heat the whole pesto batch in a saucepan.

troubleshooting.cause: Garlic size and strength vary within the listed one-to-two-clove range.
troubleshooting.fix: Use mild fresh garlic, choosing one or two cloves within the listed range. More salt does not remove a strong garlic flavor.

substitutions.alternative: Use the same listed weight range of Grana Padano.
substitutions.effect: The Pro Loco Genova recipe permits Grana Padano in the same weight range; salt and aroma differ. Keep the full listed Fiore Sardo range.

learning.timing: Allow 10–15 minutes to wash and dry the leaves, grate the cheeses and peel the garlic, followed by about 15–25 minutes of mortar work: 25–40 minutes active and elapsed. Mortar capacity determines the number of loads; allow time for each load and for pasta service separately.
learning.storage: Refrigerate freshly made pesto promptly in a clean covered container at 40°F / 4°C or below, within 2 hours of preparation or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Use within 3 days. Freeze for longer storage in suitable containers with 1/2-inch headspace, label and date, and thaw in the refrigerator. An oil layer does not make this uncooked garlic-and-herb sauce shelf-stable.

ingredients: 60–70 g fresh Genovese basil leaves, weighed without stalks; wash and dry gently
60–80 ml mild extra-virgin olive oil, preferably from the Ligurian Riviera
reserved pasta cooking water, as needed to loosen the pesto at serving, optional

exactAfter.body:
## Chef's Note

Pesto alla genovese is Liguria’s raw basil sauce, worked with garlic, pine nuts, two aged cheeses and mild olive oil. Gentle crushing and oil added at the end produce a cohesive sauce. Loosen the serving portion with pasta water and dress the pasta off the heat.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the leaves and cheeses:** Wash fresh Genovese basil leaves under running water and dry them carefully on a clean towel. Finely grate the cheeses and peel the garlic. Use a clean marble mortar and wooden pestle with room to work; divide a larger batch into mortar loads rather than filling it to the rim.
2. **Crush the garlic and pine nuts:** Put raw pine nuts and garlic cloves in the mortar. Crush the garlic to a paste, then work in the pine nuts until they form a thick paste.
3. **Work in the basil:** Add fresh Genovese basil leaves and coarse sea salt, feeding in the leaves a little at a time with the salt. Press and rotate the pestle gently against the mortar walls until the leaves form an even bright green paste. Scrape the sides as needed and work steadily without letting the mixture become warm.
4. **Add both cheeses:** Work in Parmigiano-Reggiano and Fiore Sardo until evenly distributed. Keep the full listed amounts of both cheeses.
5. **Finish with olive oil:** Drizzle in mild extra-virgin olive oil, stirring until the pesto is cohesive and creamy. Scrape into a small bowl for immediate use or a clean covered container for refrigeration.
6. **Dress the pasta off the heat:** When serving with pasta, add reserved pasta cooking water (if using) a little at a time to loosen the pesto, then toss with drained pasta in a bowl off the heat. Thin only the amount being served. Keep the remaining pesto cold.

## Cooking Notes

Use a mortar with room to work and divide the listed quantities into separate loads as needed. Choose the basil, cheese and oil amounts within their listed ranges; keep the full listed salt and pine nuts.

Refrigerate promptly at 40°F / 4°C or below and use within 3 days, or freeze for longer storage. Keep only the serving portion at the table.

sourceDecisions.before: Absent. Earlier private alternative uses a distinct Basilico Genovese DOP consortium formula; neither that formula nor the 10 g restaurant formula is a prior public recipe.
sourceDecisions.after: Entire current World Pesto Championship formula: 60–70 g basil leaves, 30 g pine nuts, 45–60 g Parmigiano-Reggiano or Grana Padano, 20–40 g Fiore Sardo, 1–2 garlic cloves, 3 g coarse salt, 60–80 ml extra-virgin olive oil. One mortar batch; no diners or volume inferred.
sourceDecisions.rationale: A complete current regional competition primary source provides measured ingredients and a full mortar sequence. Use it whole without combining the older consortium or restaurant versions.
sourceDecisions.confidence: high for faithful transmission; ranges intentionally preserved

sourceDecisions.before: Academy Sapore di Pane, Pro Loco and Genoa Chamber restaurant formula each print 10 g coarse salt while the method says a few grains. Matching publications may transmit the same restaurant recipe.
sourceDecisions.after: Current championship explicitly prints 3 g. This is a distinct whole source formula, not a silent reduction of the printed 10 g recipe. Retain the 10 g formula and consortium pinch-salt recipe as explicit comparisons.
sourceDecisions.rationale: Three matching publications establish transmission, not independent sensory validation or salt suitability. Both cheeses contribute salt. No tested flavor or health claim is made.
sourceDecisions.confidence: high that quantities differ; actual flavor suitability unmeasured

sourceDecisions.before: Ingredients list 1–2 garlic cloves; step two names one clove. Salt ingredient says 3 g; mortar method refers to some grains. Basil weight is explicitly 60–70 g for four bunches.
sourceDecisions.after: Use all the garlic chosen within the explicit 1–2 range at the garlic/pine-nut stage and all 3 g salt during gradual basil additions. Preserve every source range and use leaf weight without a new bunch conversion.
sourceDecisions.rationale: Ingredient ledger controls complete consumption; the full source method has enough room for staged basil/salt additions. This allocation decision is explicit and should receive independent review.
sourceDecisions.confidence: high for formula; moderate for full allocation reconciliation

sourceDecisions.before: No measured portion or volume yield on the championship recipe page; regional restaurant identifies a mortar batch.
sourceDecisions.after: Formula yields one batch, with no diner count or volume invented. Private preview uses an in-memory batch unit mapping; root must support the canonical batch unit and recompile before public integration.
sourceDecisions.rationale: A mortar batch represents the authored formula without inventing diners. No runtime source or public file was edited by this author.

sourceDecisions.before: Complete six-step mortar sequence; source does not establish preserved shelf stability.
sourceDecisions.after: Full mortar main with oil last; pasta-water service off heat from regional source; three-day refrigeration and freezing from NCHFP, FDA prompt cold handling.
sourceDecisions.rationale: Use authoritative preparation-specific safety rather than infer protection from an oil layer. Any optional blender route is not needed for this complete mortar recipe.
